content.overview: When a winding-up order has been made, or a provisional liquidator appointed, no suit or other legal proceeding shall be proceeded with by or against the company except with the leave of the Tribunal.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 279 (Stay of suits). When a winding-up order has been made, or a provisional liquidator appointed, no suit or other legal proceeding shall be proceeded with by or against the company except with the leave of the Tribunal. Apply only the conditions, approvals, filings and penalties stated in the section. A rule made under the Act cannot contradict the section. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: When a winding-up order has been made, or a provisional liquidator appointed, no suit or other legal proceeding shall be proceeded with by or against the company except with the leave of the Tribunal.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: Leave is the gate. The section does not bar criminal proceedings. It is the company-liquidation equivalent of a moratorium, and it is distinct from the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code moratorium.
